key_insight: Human–AI interactions do more than help us complete tasks: they can change how people see themselves and how they connect with others. The paper argues that AI systems are actively reshaping identity, behavior, and social relationships, not just decision-making.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the gap between technical AI evaluation and the broader human effects of AI use. It focuses on how repeated interaction with AI can influence self-perception, social behavior, and network dynamics in ways that are often overlooked in model-centric research.
method: Conceptual/model-based synthesis of evidence on human–AI interaction effects on the self and social networks.
Frames AI as a socio-technical agent and maps pathways from interaction patterns to psychological and social outcomes.
Identifies key mechanisms and implications for designing and studying AI systems in real-world settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that model performance is only part of the story: user experience, identity effects, and social spillovers matter too. It encourages designing systems with human well-being, social context, and long-term behavioral impact in mind.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing AI interaction -> self-perception changes -> social behavior/network changes
Three-circle Venn diagram for self, AI system, and social network
Icon set for identity, communication, and relationship shifts
Simple causal pathway chart summarizing positive and negative downstream effects
paper_title: Human–AI interactions reshape the self and our social networks
paper_authors: Andreia Sofia Teixeira, Sukhwinder Singh Shergill, Guy Laban
